title: Very early days
art_brief: Bumpy curled up asleep inside a small cut-paper acorn cup tucked among a few paper leaves on soft paper ground, with a pale paper sky by day and a dark sky with one small paper star by night.
bumpy_line: Hi. I'm very new and very small. We can take this one quiet day at a time.

know.text: Feeling tired, or even exhausted, is common in the early weeks. Rest when you can, and if it is hard going, your doctor or midwife can talk it through with you.
know.source_title: Tiredness and sleep problems in pregnancy

ready.text: Think of one person you could lean on, if and when you want to. Who you tell, and when, is your choice.
ready.suggested_question: When is my first appointment, and who do I contact if I'm worried before then?

look_forward.text: Small comforts count here: a warm drink, an early night, a kind message. Bumpy will be right here for each one.

curious.question: Which vitamin is worth taking in these early weeks?

title: Little sips
art_brief: Bumpy sitting on the rim of a big cut-paper teacup on a paper saucer, with a curl of paper steam rising beside them, under a pale paper sky by day and a deep blue sky with a paper moon by night.
bumpy_line: Some days are wobbly ones. I'm here for the wobbly days and the steady ones. Little sips, little steps.

know.text: Feeling sick is common in these weeks, and it can happen at any time of day, not only mornings. If you cannot keep food or drink down, contact your doctor or midwife.

ready.text: Keep a glass or bottle of water within reach, by the bed or in your bag. Sipping little and often can feel easier than big drinks.
ready.suggested_question: What can I try if I feel sick a lot, and when is it worth calling you?

look_forward.text: Notice any foods or drinks that sit gently on the harder days, and keep them close. Little finds like that count.

curious.question: Does sipping water help when I feel sick?

title: Tuning in
art_brief: Bumpy curled up holding one end of a paper tin-can telephone, its string looping out of the picture toward a few folded paper music notes, under a pale paper sky by day and a deep blue sky with paper stars by night.
bumpy_line: Hello out there! My ears are getting ready. Hum me something, any tune at all.

know.text: Official guides differ on when hearing begins, from around now to a few weeks later. Once it does, your baby may pick up your heartbeat, the gurgles of your tummy and voices close by.
know.source_title: 15 weeks pregnant guide - Best Start in Life - NHS

ready.text: Choose a song, rhyme or story you like and keep it handy to share with your bump. Anyone close to you can join in. No voice is too off-key.
ready.suggested_question: When might my baby start to hear the songs and voices I share?

look_forward.text: Around now, some parents give their bump a nickname, and it can start to feel like a little someone. Bumpy thinks nicknames are a wonderful idea.

curious.question: Why does folic acid matter so much for my baby's brain?

title: Swinging along
art_brief: Bumpy sitting on a cut-paper swing hanging by two paper ropes from a simple paper tree branch, mid-swing, with a paper sun and clouds by day and a dark sky with paper stars by night.
bumpy_line: Wheee! I'm swinging into the middle months. Hold on to something cozy and swing along with me.

know.text: Gums are more likely to get red and swollen during pregnancy. Regular dental care is safe at any stage of pregnancy, so it is fine to keep up your check-ups.

ready.text: If you have a dentist, give them a quick call to say you are pregnant and ask about a check-up. A small errand, done whenever suits you.
ready.suggested_question: Is it okay to go ahead with dental check-ups, and is there anything my dentist ought to know?

look_forward.text: For many parents, sickness starts to ease and energy lifts a little in the middle months. If yours has not yet, that is common too.

curious.question: I still feel tired a lot. Could low iron be part of it?

title: Middle of the map
art_brief: Bumpy sitting right at the centre fold of an open paper map, beside a tiny paper flag on a dotted path that runs from one edge of the map to the other, under a paper sun by day and a paper moon by night.
bumpy_line: Look at us, right in the middle of the map! I'm busy wiggling, napping and listening for you.

know.text: Around now, your baby moves around a lot, even if you cannot feel it yet, and is settling into waking and sleeping times of their own. Their busy times may not match yours, and that is common.
know.source_title: 21 weeks pregnant guide - Best Start in Life - NHS

ready.text: A mid-pregnancy scan is often offered around now. You can ask what it looks at, if someone can come with you, and if you can find out the sex.
ready.suggested_question: When might I start feeling my baby move, and who do I call if I'm ever unsure?

look_forward.text: The middle of the map is a fine spot for a photo of your bump, or of anything that marks this time. Yours to keep or share.

curious.question: I feel tired a lot these days. What can help me rest?

title: Peeking out
art_brief: Bumpy peeking out from between two cut-paper curtains at a small round paper window, with a paper sun shining through by day and a paper moon behind soft paper clouds by night.
bumpy_line: Peekaboo! My eyes are getting ready to open. Blinking is next on my list.

know.text: Towards the end of these weeks or soon after, your baby's eyes begin to open for the first time, and blinking comes next. There is a lot of busy activity going on in there.
know.source_title: 26 weeks pregnant guide - Best Start in Life - NHS

ready.text: Think of one thing that would really help you in the months ahead, and tell someone close. A meal, a lift, a listening ear.
ready.suggested_question: What checks or tests are coming up in the next few weeks, and what are they for?

look_forward.text: A first tiny outfit, new, borrowed or handed down, is a sweet thing to spot or set aside, whenever you feel ready. Bumpy votes for anything soft.

curious.question: Is folic acid the only thing that matters for my baby's brain?

title: Stepping stones
art_brief: Bumpy hopping across a row of round cut-paper stepping stones over a wavy paper stream with paper reeds on the bank, under a paper sun by day and a dark sky with tiny paper fireflies by night.
bumpy_line: Hop, hop! We're stepping into the last part of our story together. I'm glad you're here.

know.text: These weeks fall within the time a whooping cough vaccine is offered in pregnancy, if you have not had it yet. Your body passes protection to your baby before birth, which helps protect them early in life.

ready.text: Start a short list of who you might like with you at the birth, and anything you would like them to know. Change it any time.
ready.suggested_question: Who can be with me at the birth, and can I change my mind closer to the day?

look_forward.text: A short note to your baby, about an ordinary day or a hope, makes a lovely keepsake if you feel like writing one. Bumpy is all ears.

curious.question: My vitamin is a gummy one. Is anything missing from it?

title: Making the nest
art_brief: Bumpy tucked into a round cut-paper bird's nest lined with paper leaves and a tiny folded paper blanket, resting on a paper branch, with a pale sky by day and a paper crescent moon and small glowing paper lantern by night.
bumpy_line: Getting snug in here! Tell me about the world out there. Is it noisy, quiet, full of birds? I'm curious.

know.text: Babies keep moving right up to birth. If your baby is moving less than usual, has stopped, or their pattern changes, call your doctor or midwife or the hospital straight away, even at night.

ready.text: Some swelling in feet, ankles and fingers is common now, often worse by evening. Putting feet up can help. Sudden swelling is different: see When to get help right away.
ready.suggested_question: Where do I go, and who do I call, when labour starts or if something feels different?

look_forward.text: Many parents start to picture the first hello around now. Daydream about it as much or as little as you like. Bumpy is daydreaming too.

curious.question: My baby is storing calcium now. Where can I get mine?

title: Bag by the door
art_brief: Bumpy peeking out of a small open cut-paper bag that sits beside a simple paper door with a round paper knob, lit by a pale paper sun by day and a small paper wall lamp by night.
bumpy_line: Pack a snack for me? Just kidding, I've got everything I want in here. Still growing, still listening.

know.text: Your baby's brain, lungs, liver and other important organs are still developing in these last weeks of pregnancy. There is plenty of growing still going on in there.
know.source_title: Why at least 39 weeks is best for your baby

ready.text: Pack a small bag with a few comfy things you already have: something soft to wear, a snack, a phone charger and anything that soothes you.
ready.suggested_question: How will I know when it's time to come in, and what is worth bringing?

look_forward.text: Many parents start trying out names around now, out loud, in whispers, or not yet at all. Bumpy is listening for favourites.

curious.question: With all these trips to the loo, how can I tell if I'm drinking enough?

title: In good time
art_brief: Bumpy resting in a cut-paper hammock slung between two simple paper trees, with a paper sunrise behind them by day and a paper crescent moon with a few paper stars by night.
bumpy_line: Still in here, still listening. I'm keeping you company, one day at a time.

know.text: If labour has not started on its own around now, your doctor or midwife will talk through all your options with you. The choice of what happens next is yours.

ready.text: Pick a few gentle things for the waiting days: a short walk, a film, a call with a friend, a nap. Easy plans, easy to cancel.
ready.suggested_question: If my baby hasn't arrived yet, what are my options, and what would you suggest for me?

look_forward.text: Each waiting day brings the first hello a little closer. Until then, Bumpy is right here, keeping you company.

curious.question: How can I rest well while I wait?
